log: Starting RT applies to ALL units (players and enemies) + Player Initiative Edge (10 RT)

LUK Initiative is SYMMETRIC: players and enemies use the SAME formula. STEP 1 (every unit, once, at initial deployment): LUK Starting RT = round(Base RT × (1 − 0.30 × LUK / (100 + LUK))). Base RT input: player units = standard 400; enemy units = their tier base RT (current: Grunt 400, Veteran 380, Elite 350). STEP 2 (PLAYER-ROSTER units only) — Player Initiative Edge: Starting RT = LUK Starting RT − 10 (minimum 1). The edge is applied LAST, after any percentage Starting-RT modifiers (e.g. traits such as Timeline Sovereign / Temporal Drag). It does NOT apply to enemies, neutrals, allied NPCs, summons, or mid-battle reinforcements. Examples at LUK 10: Player 400 → 389 → 379; Grunt 400 → 389; Veteran 380 → 370; Elite 350 → 340. At LUK 50: Player 400 → 360 → 350; Grunt 400 → 360; Elite 350 → 315.

USER RULING 2026-10-02 (revises the same-day Designer ruling that had full parity and no player edge): LUK initiative applies to enemies too, keeping only a MINIMAL player-only advantage. Designer-chosen edge = flat 10 RT. Why 10, and why flat: (1) 10 RT = 2.5% of a 400 RT turn, 1% of a 1000-CT round — at equal LUK and tier the player simply moves first, so mirror matchups open in the player's favour; (2) it never overturns enemy tier identity — a LUK-10 player (379) still acts after a LUK-10 Veteran (370) or Elite (340); (3) it is the same size at every LUK, so LUK is worth exactly the same to both sides (a stronger player-only LUK coefficient was rejected: zero edge for low-LUK players, and LUK would be worth more on players than enemies — re-creating the asymmetry); (4) it is worth only ~10 LUK at low LUK, so a slightly luckier enemy can still beat it. SUPERSEDES the Sep 28 2026 'flagged, undecided' asymmetry note and this row's earlier no-edge wording. DEV CHANGE PENDING (Dev agent): EnemyGenerator sets startingRt = tier.baseRt and ignores LUK — it must apply STEP 1 to enemies; the player deploy path must add STEP 2. Until then shipped code is asymmetric. Not Studio-tested.

THREE-LAYER RT MODEL (USER RULING 2026-10-04 — final; supersedes the prior Starting-RT basis). LAYER 1 — Base RT = the unit's own base value + Effective Armor WT (gear). Own base value: player units = 400; enemy units = their KIND base (Grunt 400 / Veteran 380 / Elite 350), set BEFORE gear WT and BEFORE any modifier. LAYER 2 — Modified Base RT = Layer-1 Base RT × permanent trait base-RT modifiers (e.g. Quick −10%, Sluggish +10%, Timeline Sovereign −10%, Temporal Drag +8%) × active temporary RT statuses (Haste ×0.90, Slow ×1.10, Frozen ×2). Every Base-RT-derived per-turn cost (Move, Basic Attack, Guard, Interact, Item, Push, Rest) is calculated from Modified Base RT — see weapons_equipment 'Modified Base RT'. LAYER 3 — ONE-TIME modifiers: Starting RT is NOT a standalone or persistent stat. It is a one-time reduction applied to the unit's current RT once, at initial deployment, to decide who takes the first turn. STEP 1 (every unit, players and enemies, SAME formula): Starting RT = round(Modified Base RT × (1 − 0.30 × LUK / (100 + LUK)) × (1 + Trait Starting-RT %)). The Base RT INPUT is the unit's MODIFIED Base RT at deployment (includes Effective Armor WT, permanent trait modifiers, and any Haste/Slow/Frozen active at deploy) — NOT plain 400 / plain kind base. Trait Starting-RT %: Timeline Sovereign −12%, Temporal Drag +15%, otherwise 0 (if several ever apply, add the percentages). STEP 2 (PLAYER-ROSTER units only) — Player Initiative Edge: Starting RT = STEP-1 result − 10 (minimum 1), applied LAST, after LUK and trait percentages. No edge for enemies, neutrals, allied NPCs, summons, or mid-battle reinforcements. After the opener, RT follows normal per-turn costs from Modified Base RT; Starting RT never recurs. Examples at LUK 10 (WT = Effective Armor WT): Player WT 0: 400 → 389 → 379. Player WT 30: 430 → 418 → 408. Player WT 30 + Haste at deploy: 387 → 376 → 366. Grunt WT 0: 400 → 389; Grunt WT 20: 420 → 409. Veteran WT 0: 380 → 370; Veteran WT 20: 400 → 389. Elite WT 0: 350 → 340; Elite WT 20: 370 → 360; Elite WT 60: 410 → 399. Timeline Sovereign player WT 0: 360 → 308 → 298. Temporal Drag player WT 0: 432 → 483 → 473. At LUK 50: Player WT 0: 400 → 360 → 350; Player WT 30: 430 → 387 → 377; Elite WT 0: 350 → 315.

USER RULING 2026-10-04 (final; SUPERSEDES the 2026-10-02 STEP-1 basis 'player units = standard 400; enemy units = their tier base RT'). Source code already implements this model (Tester source-UAT 2026-10-04), except the trait Starting-RT % below. SUPERSEDED: prior examples that excluded armor from Starting RT (e.g. Elite 350 → 340 quoted regardless of gear) — Starting RT derives from Modified Base RT. 350 → 340 is still correct only for an Elite with 0 Effective Armor WT and no modifiers. Enemy kind identity is preserved by the Base-RT layering (at equal gear and LUK: Elite < Veteran < Grunt), but a heavily-armored unit can legitimately start later than a lighter unit of a faster kind (e.g. Elite WT 60 = 399 starts after an unarmored LUK-10 player at 379) — ACCEPTED by user ruling. Kind base RT now affects EVERY per-turn cost, not just the first turn (previously only the opener): e.g. Veteran Basic Attack base component round(380×0.10) = 38 vs 40; Veteran Rest round(380×0.75) = 285 vs 300; Elite movement 350×0.03 = 10.5 RT/tile vs 12 (before AGI). KEPT from 2026-10-02 ruling: symmetric LUK formula; flat −10 RT Player Initiative Edge, players only, applied last (10 RT = 2.5% of a 400 RT turn; same size at every LUK; worth ~10 LUK, so a luckier enemy can still beat it). TRAIT STARTING-RT % — Designer canon 2026-10-04, INTENDED BEHAVIOUR, DEV CHANGE PENDING: Timeline Sovereign / Temporal Drag Base-RT parts (−10% / +8%) are WIRED and live in Layer 2, so they already flow into the Starting-RT input. Their Starting-RT parts (−12% / +15%) ALSO layer on, as a multiplier inside the STEP-1 one-time reduction (after LUK, before the Player Edge, one rounding). This deliberately stacks with the Base-RT part: Sovereign opens ~21% earlier than an equal unit (298 vs 379), Drag ~25% later (473 vs 379). Accepted because it only affects the opener, the pair is legendary-tier, and the separate Starting-RT line is the trait's 'Timeline' identity. If playtest shows Sovereign openers are too dominant, retune the −12% (not the model). Not Studio-tested.

Modified Base RT = (unit's own Base RT + Effective Armor WT) × permanent trait base-RT modifiers × active Haste (×0.90) / Slow (×1.10) / Frozen (×2). Unit's own Base RT (Layer 1): player units 400; enemy units = their KIND base — Grunt 400 / Veteran 380 / Elite 350 (not a flat 400); boss units 300 (core_stats 'Boss unit'). Effective Armor WT = non-weapon equipment WT (Body/Head/Gloves/Feet/Accessory) after STR burden reduction; Armor Off-Hand WT is excluded (project_rules 'Armor Off-Hand WT'). Every Base-RT-derived per-turn cost (Move, Basic Attack, Guard, Interact, Item, Push, Rest) uses this value, so enemy kind base RT flows into every turn. It is also the input to the one-time Starting RT reduction (core_stats 'Starting RT applies to ALL units').

USER RULING 2026-10-04 (three-layer RT model, final): clarified the kind-base input and modifier order. Previous text was 'Base RT + Effective Armor WT.', which implied a flat 400 base for everyone. Weapon BP pricing references (Two-Attack Cycle RT, Attacks per 1000 CT) still assume a 400-base player unit.
LUK (Combat Fortune, Initiative, Discovery Radius, deterministic tie-breaking, expedition rewards)

Combat Fortune Modifier = 0.40 x Delta LUK / (abs(Delta LUK) + 150)
Starting RT = round(Base RT x (1 - 0.30 x LUK / (100 + LUK)))
Discovery Radius = 1 + floor(LUK / 60) + Bonuses - Penalties
Unit Fortune = LUK / (LUK + 200)

At +/-150 LUK difference, Combat Fortune changes direct final damage by +/-20%. Initiative applies once at initial deployment. LUK does not modify Hit Quality, status application, or recruitment.
